parameters.name: n_estimators
parameters.override_rationale: Excessive boosting iterations on a small dataset lead to overfitting, even with early stopping. Capping n_estimators at 200 prevents the model from over-specializing to the training folds.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.override_rationale: With only 312 samples, deep trees will severely overfit by memorizing noise. Constraining max_depth to a maximum of 5 forces the model to learn only the most robust, high-level composition-property relationships.

parameters.name: num_leaves
parameters.override_rationale: LightGBM's primary complexity driver is num_leaves. Capping it at 31 (which corresponds roughly to a max_depth of 5) ensures the model remains constrained and generalizes well to the 42 features.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.override_rationale: Similar to XGBoost, LightGBM needs strict depth constraints on 312 samples to prevent the leaf-wise growth algorithm from creating overly complex, overfitted trees.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.override_rationale: While Random Forest is more robust to overfitting than boosting, allowing unlimited depth on 312 samples with 42 features can still increase variance. Capping at 12 provides enough capacity for non-linear interactions while maintaining stability.

trial_allocation.allocation_rationale: Baseline model — fixed defaults, no HPO needed.

XGBoost is highly sensitive to hyperparameters like max_depth, learning_rate, and n_estimators. Given the small dataset (312 samples), it requires careful tuning to find the narrow sweet spot that captures non-linearities without overfitting. 18 trials allow sufficient exploration of the constrained search space.

LightGBM's leaf-wise growth mechanism makes it prone to overfitting on small datasets if num_leaves and max_depth are not tightly controlled. 15 trials provide enough budget to tune its regularization parameters (lambda_l1, lambda_l2) and tree structure constraints.

Random Forest is inherently more robust to overfitting due to bagging and feature subsampling. It requires less aggressive HPO than gradient boosting models, so 10 trials are sufficient to optimize max_depth and min_samples_split for the 42 features.

Elastic Net has a very small search space (primarily alpha and l1_ratio). 7 trials are more than enough to map the convex optimization landscape and find the optimal regularization balance for the 42 features.

checklist.comment: All candidate models (ridge, xgboost, lightgbm, random_forest, elastic_net) natively support regression. MAE is a valid regression metric.
Ridge regression serves as a solid linear baseline for regression, providing a meaningful reference point for evaluating HPO-tuned tree-based and regularized models.

50 total trials across 4 HPO-enabled models (~12 trials each) is reasonable for a small dataset of 312 samples. Excessive trials on small data could cause validation set overfitting, so this budget is appropriately conservative.
K-fold cross-validation is well-suited for a dataset with only 312 samples, maximizing data usage for both training and evaluation.
Primary metric (MAE) and evaluation metric (MAE) are aligned. No inconsistency detected.

With 312 samples and 42 features (ratio ~7.4:1), tree-based models under HPO may overfit to cross-validation folds. The risk is mitigated by k-fold CV and conservative trial budget but remains present.
50 HPO trials on 312 samples with 42 features is computationally lightweight. No resource concerns anticipated.
Optuna TPE is a well-defined, reproducible search method. Pipeline structure is clear. Explicit seed documentation would further strengthen reproducibility.

non_blocking_risks.message: The feature-to-sample ratio (42 features / 312 samples ≈ 0.135) is moderately high for tree-based ensemble methods. HPO may exploit noise in small validation folds, leading to optimistic performance estimates that do not generalize.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Monitor gap between CV MAE and any held-out test MAE. Consider constraining tree depth or minimum samples per leaf in HPO search spaces to regularize tree-based models.

non_blocking_risks.message: Three of the four HPO candidates are tree-based ensemble methods (xgboost, lightgbm, random_forest), which may yield correlated predictions and limit the benefit of running all three.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Consider whether all three tree-based models are necessary, or reallocate some trials to explore different model families (e.g., kernel methods, neural approaches) if the task warrants it.

future_improvement_suggestions: Consider applying feature selection or dimensionality reduction (e.g., variance thresholding, mutual information) given the moderate feature-to-sample ratio to reduce overfitting risk.
Consider nested cross-validation (outer loop for evaluation, inner loop for HPO) to obtain a less biased estimate of generalization performance on this small dataset.
Document explicit random seeds for Optuna sampler, model initialization, and data splitting to ensure full reproducibility across runs.
Consider adding a non-regularized linear regression or simple decision tree as an additional naive baseline to better contextualize the gains from HPO.
